01

About the application

Plum Guide is a demonstration of a curated holiday-home platform. Every home in the public collection has been inspected and scored by a Plum specialist. Guests can check live availability and book instantly; hosts manage their calendar and prices; specialists record inspections; administrators oversee the whole operation.

What you can do

  • Search a collection of approved homes only
  • See live availability, custom nightly prices and the full quote
  • Book, receive a reference and print an invoice
  • Cancel and see the refund before confirming
  • Hosts submit homes and schedule the Plum Test
  • Specialists publish slots and score inspections
  • Admins review inspections and override refunds

Before you start

  • A current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari
  • A screen at least 360 px wide; the portals are responsive
  • One of the demo accounts below, or a new guest/host account
  • For local use: Node.js 22.19 or newer and npm

This is a teaching demonstration. Payments are simulated; do not enter real card details or personal data.

Prices and currencyAll nightly rates, fees, invoices and refunds are shown in euros (€). A banner at the top of every public page confirms “Now in euros”. Amounts are authored in EUR; the app does not perform live currency conversion.

02

Accessing the application

Option A — run it locally (recommended for the full demo)

  1. Check the runtime. Open a terminal and run node -v. You need Node.js 22.19 or newer (the build was tested on Node 24). Install Node.js from nodejs.org if needed.
  2. Install dependencies. From the project root run npm install. This also generates the Prisma client.
  3. Create the local environment file. Run cp .env.example .env, then set a long random value for AUTH_SECRET. Local development can use the built-in fallback, but setting it avoids session surprises. Generate one with openssl rand -base64 32.
  4. Start the app. Run npm run dev. The server listens on http://localhost:3000. Next.js starts a local Cloudflare D1 database through Wrangler using freebuff.wrangler.jsonc.
  5. Open the site. Visit http://localhost:3000. The first request creates the schema, indexes, guard trigger and demo data. Give it a few seconds; later requests are immediate.
npm install
cp .env.example .env
npm run dev
# http://localhost:3000
Fresh startLocal data lives in .wrangler/state. Stop the server, delete that folder, and start again to recreate the demo database. This discards bookings and changes you made.

Option B — use a hosted demonstration

If your instructor or team supplied a deployed URL, open it in a current browser. No installation is required. Hosted environments share the same demo accounts and reset policy as the local build. If a hosted copy shows old pound (£) prices, it is serving a previous deployment: ask the owner to redeploy the current build rather than changing your browser settings.

03

Signing in and out

  1. Select Sign in in the top-right of the public site. The login page opens.
  2. Enter your email address and password, or choose a Demo account card to fill the form. The cards are labelled Guest, Host, Specialist and Admin.
  3. Press Sign in. You are redirected to the dashboard for your role. If you arrived from a protected page, you return there after signing in.
  4. To leave, press Sign out in the header. The session cookie is cleared and you return to the home page.

Creating an account: choose Join Plum, enter your full name, email and a password of at least 8 characters, then select Guest (book stays) or Host (submit a home). You are signed in immediately. An existing email cannot be registered twice.

04

Guest tasks

4.1 Browse and search the collection

  1. Open Homes from the header, or the Explore vetted homes button on the home page.
  2. Type a place or home name in Where to? — for example Amalfi, London or Provence — and press Search homes. Search matches the title and location.
  3. Use Sort by to choose Curator’s pick, Price: low to high or Price: high to low.
  4. Select a home card to open its detail page. Every card shows the Plum score and the nightly rate in euros.

4.2 Book a stay

  1. On the property page, review the Plum score, description, capacity and house details. The booking panel is on the right (below the images on a phone).
  2. Choose a check-in date in the calendar. Unavailable nights are struck through and disabled; past dates are disabled.
  3. Choose a check-out date. The nights in between are highlighted and the quote appears: nightly subtotal, cleaning fee, service fee and total.
  4. Check the total and press Confirm & Pay. If you are not signed in, you are taken to sign-in first; after signing in, return to the home and confirm. Stays are limited to 30 nights.
  5. The confirmation page opens with a reference such as PLM-E2C8A42. Keep it for support. The dates are now held and cannot be booked by anyone else.
Why a date is unavailableThe host may have closed it, or another guest may already hold it. The calendar combines both sources, so a struck-through night cannot be booked even if it looks free elsewhere.

4.3 Confirmation and invoice

After booking you land on the confirmation page. It shows the reference, home, dates, guest, price breakdown and total paid. Press View invoice for the printable invoice, or open it later from Dashboard → My trips → Download invoice.

4.4 Cancel a reservation

  1. Open Dashboard and find the reservation under Upcoming trips, or use the cancellation button on the confirmation page.
  2. Press Cancel reservation. A dialog shows the stay, the estimated refund, the percentage and the policy tier that applies.
  3. Enter a reason of at least 10 characters. This is shared with the concierge team.
  4. Press Confirm cancellation. The reservation becomes Cancelled, the refund is recorded and every night is released back to the calendar immediately.
Cancellation is finalA cancelled booking cannot be restored. The dates return to the host’s calendar as soon as the cancellation completes; you would need to book again. The policy is: 100% refund more than 14 days before check-in, 50% at 7–14 days, and no refund under 7 days.

4.5 Review past trips

The guest dashboard separates Upcoming trips from Past & cancelled stays. Each row shows the reference, dates, total, status and refund (if any), with a link to the invoice.

05

Host tasks

The host portal shows total revenue, upcoming revenue, confirmed bookings and how many homes are approved. Below the metrics, Your homes lists every listing with its status and a Manage calendar action.

5.1 Add a home

  1. Press Add a home in the host portal (or List your home on the public site).
  2. Enter a listing title, location, nightly rate in euros, bedrooms, bathrooms, maximum guests and an optional description. The rate must be between €50 and €100,000.
  3. Choose one of the editorial cover images. Uploads are not part of the demonstration.
  4. Press Save draft & choose inspection. The home is created as a Draft and is not visible to guests.

5.2 Schedule the Plum Test

  1. On the listing’s management page, find the Plum Test panel.
  2. Choose an available specialist slot from the list and press Schedule Plum Test. The panel changes to Inspection booked and shows the date and specialist.
  3. The specialist visits, records a score and notes. A score of 85 or above approves the home automatically; below 85 it is referred to the curation team, who may still override.
  4. Approved homes appear in the public collection immediately. You can then open the public listing from the management page.
No slots available?Slots are published by specialists. If the list is empty, check back later or contact the specialist team; a host cannot create a specialist slot.

5.3 Manage availability and prices

  1. Press Manage calendar on a home. The Availability & pricing calendar opens on the next 365 days.
  2. Select a date. Choose Open for bookings or Closed to guests.
  3. Optionally enter a Custom nightly price in euros. Leave it blank to use the base rate; the placeholder shows the base rate.
  4. Press Save date. A gold dot marks dates with a custom price. Use Reset price to return a date to the base rate.
Reserved nightsA night held by a confirmed booking is shown as reserved and cannot be reopened or repriced. It returns to your calendar automatically when the guest cancels.

5.4 Edit the listing title or base rate

In Listing details, change the title or base nightly rate in euros and press Save listing details. The base rate applies to every night without a custom price; existing bookings keep the total they were charged.

06

Specialist tasks

  1. Publish availability. In Publish an inspection slot, choose a date and a start time (UK time). Slots are 90 minutes. Press Publish slot; hosts can now claim it.
  2. Check your diary. Booked inspections appear under Upcoming home inspections with the home, location and host contact details. Open Open audit form when you have completed the visit.
  3. Record the result. Enter a Plum Test score from 0 to 100 and inspection notes of at least 10 characters. Press Record Plum Test result.
  4. Automatic outcome. A score of 85 or above approves the home; below 85 rejects it and sends it to the admin review queue. The result appears in Completed inspections.
  5. Withdraw an unclaimed slot with the Withdraw button. A slot already booked by a host cannot be withdrawn.
Top ↑

07

Administrator tasks

The admin portal shows gross booking value, approved homes, inspection pipeline, cancellation rate, refunds issued and member counts. Scroll for the review queue, recent bookings and cancellations.

7.1 Review an inspection

  1. Find the home under Inspection review queue. The latest inspection, specialist and score are shown.
  2. Press Approve to publish the home, or Reject to keep it out of the collection.
  3. Reject asks for confirmation a second time: press Yes, reject to complete, or Cancel to keep the current status.

7.2 Override a refund

  1. Scroll to Cancellations & refund overrides and find the cancellation.
  2. Enter a new refund amount in the field (euros) and press Override refund. The amount cannot exceed the booking total.
  3. The cancellation is marked Admin override, preserving the reason and the original policy percentage for audit.

08

Prices and refunds

Every price is in euros and is calculated on the server:

nightly subtotal = sum of each night's custom price, or the base rate
cleaning fee     = €180
service fee      = 8% of the nightly subtotal
total            = nightly subtotal + €180 + 8%

The quote you see before booking is the amount stored with the reservation. If a host later changes the base rate, existing bookings keep their original total.

When you cancelRefundWhat happens to the dates
More than 14 days before check-in100% of the total paidReleased immediately
7–14 days before check-in50% of the total paidReleased immediately
Fewer than 7 days before check-inNo refundReleased immediately

An administrator can override a refund for a dispute or goodwill gesture, up to the booking total. All amounts remain in EUR.

09

Troubleshooting common issues

Start with the exact message shown in the app. The table below covers the issues encountered during testing and the quickest safe fix.

Symptom or messageLikely causeWhat to do
“That email and password combination is not recognised.” Typo, wrong role password, or the local database was reset. Use the demo buttons on the sign-in page. Check Caps Lock. If you reset .wrangler/state, use the seeded accounts, not an account you created before the reset.
The page loads but no homes, users or bookings appear. The first request is still bootstrapping D1, or the local D1 state is incomplete. Wait a few seconds and reload. If it persists, stop the server, delete .wrangler/state, run npm run dev again and reload once.
Dates are struck through or cannot be selected. The host closed the night, another guest holds it, or it is in the past. Choose different nights. A night can be unavailable because of a confirmed reservation as well as a host closure.
“Those dates have just been reserved by another guest. Please choose different dates.” Another request won the race for the same night. This is the concurrency guard working as intended. Pick another range; nothing was charged or reserved for the failed attempt.
“One of those nights has just been closed by the host.” The host closed a night after the calendar was loaded. Reload the property page and pick different dates.
Confirm & Pay is greyed out. No check-out selected, or the selected range is incomplete or invalid. Select a check-in and a later check-out. The button enables only when a valid range has produced a quote. If you are signed out, the button still works and takes you to sign-in.
Clicking Confirm & Pay sends you to sign-in. Booking requires a guest session. Sign in with the guest demo account and repeat the selection. The app returns you to the same home.
“This reservation has already been cancelled.” The booking was cancelled in another tab or earlier session. Reload the dashboard. The reservation stays in Past & cancelled stays; do not try to cancel it again.
“Please add a short reason (at least 10 characters).” The cancellation reason is too short. Write at least 10 characters explaining the change of plans. This is required before the cancellation can be recorded.
A reserved night cannot be reopened. A confirmed booking holds it. Wait for the guest to cancel. If the booking is being cancelled by support, the night is released automatically in the same operation.
No specialist slots are listed when scheduling a Plum Test. No specialist has published a future, unclaimed slot. Check back later or ask a specialist to publish availability. Hosts cannot create slots themselves.
“A Plum Test is already scheduled for this home.” or “This home has passed the Plum Test.” The home already has a booked or completed inspection. Wait for the scheduled visit, or ask an administrator about a re-inspection. The panel is read-only by design.
Approve/Reject buttons are not shown. There is no completed inspection score yet. Only inspected homes can be moderated. The row shows “Awaiting inspection” until the specialist records a result.
“The refund cannot exceed the booking total…” The override is larger than the amount paid. Enter a value up to the booking total shown in the message. The cap protects the platform and the guest.
Prices still show £ or “GBP”. A hosted copy is serving an older deployment, or the browser cached an old page. Hard-reload first (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + R). If the banner is still missing, the deployment is stale; redeploy the current build. The local source uses eur() and shows EUR.
The invoice does not download as a file. The demo uses the browser’s print dialog rather than a PDF generator. Press Download / print invoice, choose Save as PDF as the destination and save. Pop-up blockers usually do not affect this because it is a print dialog.
Signed out unexpectedly after a while. The session cookie expired (7 days) or the secret changed. Sign in again. Changing AUTH_SECRET invalidates existing sessions; this is expected.
“An account already exists for that email.” The email is already registered. Sign in instead, or use a different email. Email addresses are matched case-insensitively.
The app will not start locally. Node version, missing dependencies, a port conflict, or missing D1 configuration. Run node -v (22.19+), then npm install. If port 3000 is busy, stop the other process or start with npx next dev -p 3001. Keep freebuff.wrangler.jsonc in place; the D1 binding is provided by it.
Reporting an issueInclude the page URL, the role you were signed in as, the exact message, and the booking reference if there is one. Do not include passwords or payment details.

10

Guided demonstration (about 10 minutes)

This sequence shows the whole operating loop. It is the same script used in the presentation; each step produces a visible change for the next role.

  1. Guest — book. Sign in as guest@plumguide.com. Open Homes → Villa Fico, choose two adjacent available nights and note the total. Press Confirm & Pay and keep the reference.
  2. Guest — inspect the paperwork. Open View invoice and print or save it. Then open Dashboard; the new trip is at the top of Upcoming trips.
  3. Host — manage supply. Sign out, sign in as host@plumguide.com. Open The Tuscan Farmhouse → Manage calendar. Close one future night and set a custom price on another; save both.
  4. Host — request inspection. In the Plum Test panel, choose an available slot and press Schedule Plum Test.
  5. Specialist — inspect. Sign in as specialist@plumguide.com. Publish a slot, open the booked visit and record 92 with notes. The home is approved automatically.
  6. Admin — oversee. Sign in as admin@plumguide.com. Confirm the home moved to the collection, review the queue, and try a refund override on a cancelled booking.
  7. Guest — cancel. Return to the guest account, cancel the trip from My trips, read the preview and confirm. Reopen the property calendar as the host: the released nights are open again.
Resetting between demonstrationsStop the server, delete .wrangler/state, then run npm run dev. The seed restores nine users, thirteen homes, seven bookings and the demonstration calendar. The screenshots in this guide were captured from a seeded database.

Support and glossary

TermMeaning
Plum TestThe inspection standard: 150 checks, aggregated into a score out of 100. 85 or above passes.
Plum ApprovedA home that passed inspection and appears in the public collection.
Inspection scheduledA host has claimed a specialist slot; the visit has not yet been scored.
Not approvedThe home was inspected or rejected and is not bookable. Admins can reconsider it.
DraftA new home that is not yet in the inspection pipeline and is invisible to guests.
Reserved nightA night held by a confirmed booking; shown as black in the host calendar.
Custom priceA per-night override of the base rate, marked with a gold dot.
ReferenceThe human-readable booking code, beginning PLM-.

Concierge (demonstration): concierge@plumguide.com, Monday–Friday, 9am–7pm UK time. For a real deployment, replace this with the operator’s support channel.

Demo credentialsThe seeded accounts use simple, public passwords. Never reuse them, or this configuration, in a production system. Payments and confirmation emails are simulated.
